chapter: Raymond Scott, Kirby and postwar bands
title: Preferring small bands: Hackett invites him to Nick's
summary: Tired of moving brass sections, Leeman found the pleasure of subtle small-band drumming with Kirby, and in late 1949 Bobby Hackett offers him a job at Nick's.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Anyway, you asked me how did I happen to go in the Nick's Well, Bobby Hackett too me in, but beforehand I must say, Bobby Hackett, the great trumpet player, we had been friends for years, going back to Boston, before he came to New York. The one thing that happened to me, I fell in love with little bands while playing with Kirby, but I had been -- I was sick to death of moving brass sections. Do you follow me? I was just sick to death of it, killing myself -- and all of a sudden, it came to me, once I found the secret of playing with little bands, it was a joy -- and that happened with John Kirby. You could play with a driving force with a small group, but you still keep that -- you can play subtly, rather, but you still keep that driving force. And that had to come to me, working with Kirby. As I had said, I had it with big bands, so Bobby Hackett -- I needed a job, and so Bobby Hackett had asked me, and this was late '49, if I wanted to go into Nick's with him, and I was surprised, because that was in a different groove than which I knew, musically, you know; that was a little band.
